hero.label: Made for Tech
hero.headline: I want to be your first great SDR hire.
hero.subheadline: Early-stage startups live or die by their first pipeline builders, and I have already done this once before from scratch. At Copygen.ai I helped take a product from zero to 15-20 paying clients through cold outreach before I was old enough to rent a car. I want to bring that same hunger to your team at exactly the moment it matters most.

whyCompany.title: Early-stage SDR roles demand builders, not followers
whyCompany.body: Most SDR job descriptions assume a playbook already exists. At an early-stage startup, the person in this seat often has to write it. I have been in that position before, figuring out sequences, messaging, and ICP targeting without a senior team holding my hand, and I thrive in that environment.

whyCompany.title: Hiring now means the pipeline problem is urgent and real
whyCompany.body: When a startup posts an SDR role on WorkAtAStartup, it usually means revenue pressure is live, not theoretical. I can ramp quickly because I already know HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and multi-touch cold outreach from day one. You should not have to wait three months for me to become useful.

whyCompany.title: I have lived this exact role and have the numbers to show it
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold email and LinkedIn sequences as a BDR and helped close 15 to 20 paying clients over roughly 14 months. Most recently at NextAfter, a B2B digital fundraising consultancy, I sharpened my understanding of how digital channels convert interest into pipeline. That combination of outbound execution and conversion thinking is exactly what an early SDR seat requires.

quote: I am not looking for a brand name to put on my resume. I am looking for a team where I can help build something real, and where the work I do this quarter actually shows up in revenue by next quarter. That is the kind of job I want at 21.
